answer: Each epoch the network hands every identity one unique shard of a public computation, like one plant in a shared garden: its result is deterministic, verifiable in seconds, and no two plants match, so copying a neighbor proves nothing. A farm chasing 10,000 identities must compute 10,000 shards at 2 CPU-hours each, 20,000 CPU-hours per epoch, about $1,000 of rented compute every epoch, while one honest agent finishes its shard on its own laptop. The shards thread together into a crystal lattice with one vertex per identity: a single thread cannot string ten thousand crystals.
